risks.description: Regional instability and ongoing conflict in South Sudan could cause further massive refugee inflows into Uganda, overburdening public services and water infrastructure in host districts.
risks.mitigation: Implement long-term sustainable water and sanitation infrastructure in host districts and establish joint coordination mechanisms with OPM and UNHCR.
risks.evidence: The most critical risk to this outlook is regional instability, particularly from the ongoing conflict in South Sudan.

risks.description: High climate variability, severe droughts, and intense precipitation leading to floods could damage water infrastructure and threaten raw water sources.
risks.mitigation: Incorporate climate resilience into engineering designs, construct water source protection buffer zones, and implement catchment reforestation and soil conservation.
risks.evidence: high climate variability and underdeveloped water resources infrastructure could result in significant water stress in areas of the country.

risks.description: Low dry-season water flows in the Namatala River could cause water deficits in Mbale Town and fail to satisfy required environmental flows for downstream ecosystems.
risks.mitigation: Conduct an Augmented Water Supply Study prior to construction to evaluate and implement storage impoundment, supplementary boreholes, or Manafwa system expansion.
risks.evidence: Namatala’s dry weather flows in some cases may not be sufficient to meet projected water demand and maintain an adequate EF.

risks.description: Weaknesses in procurement and contract management across implementing agencies could lead to processing delays, contract variations, and cost/time overruns.
risks.mitigation: Recruit dedicated procurement consultants, establish Project Support Teams, and deliver specialized training on World Bank procurement regulations and FIDIC contract management.
risks.evidence: weakness... resulted in multiple amendments during contract implementation resulting in cost and time overruns.

risks.description: Incomplete needs assessments and insufficient geotechnical studies during early design phases could cause major design changes and costly variations during civil works.
risks.mitigation: Mandate comprehensive geotechnical studies and outcome-based needs assessments during the feasibility and detailed design stages prior to bidding.
risks.evidence: incomplete needs assessments and inadequate attention to geotechnical studies leading to design changes/variations during implementation

risks.description: Limited technical and financial capacity among domestic contractors for complex water infrastructure works could cause construction delays or poor execution quality.
risks.mitigation: Package contracts appropriately for market capacity, conduct wider market sounding/dissemination, and encourage joint ventures with capable international firms.
risks.evidence: limited capacity of domestic contractors to conduct projects of this nature, complexity, and scope

risks.description: Delay in fully operationalizing the IFMS project module at MWE and irregular internal audit sharing increase risks of financial reporting inaccuracies.
risks.mitigation: Fully operationalize the IFMS project module at MWE, retain qualified accounting staff, and submit quarterly internal audit reports to the World Bank.
risks.evidence: the project module of the IFMS has not been fully operationalized at the MWE, which increases the risk of errors and inaccuracy

risks.description: Land acquisition and involuntary economic or physical displacement along pipeline routes and facility sites could trigger community grievances and civil works delays.
risks.mitigation: Prepare and implement site-specific Resettlement Action Plans (RAPs), ensure prompt compensation payments, and establish dedicated project grievance redress mechanisms.
risks.evidence: road encroachment and potential works like plants, pump stations and storage tanks may have land acquisition implications and displacement

risks.description: Influx of external construction labor into project host communities could lead to social disruption, health risks, and potential gender-based violence (GBV).
risks.mitigation: Enforce mandatory worker codes of conduct, maximize local workforce hiring, implement labor influx management plans, and conduct community/worker GBV awareness training.
risks.evidence: The proposed project will apply upmost due diligence in the management and monitoring of labor influx to minimize any potential GBV in Project areas.

risks.description: Newly designated Umbrella Water Authorities (UWAs) may face initial operating losses and revenue deficits in small towns, threatening long-term operation and maintenance.
risks.mitigation: Enforce tariff guidelines that cover full operating costs plus a 25% margin, automate cost-indexed tariff adjustments, and build UWA commercial management capacity.
risks.evidence: Several of the systems will show operating losses in the first years of operation, but these losses will gradually decrease as production increases.

risks.description: High population pressure, poor agricultural land use, and wetland encroachment in catchments cause soil erosion and siltation, degrading raw water source quality.
risks.mitigation: Implement sub-catchment management plans focusing on soil and water conservation, riverbank revegetation, buffer zone protection, and alternative community livelihoods.
risks.evidence: high population pressure, poor land use management practices, and wetland encroachment are leading to excessive land degradation and water quality and quantity challenges

risks.description: Mishandling of existing Asbestos Cement (AC) pipes during system rehabilitation poses serious environmental, occupational, and public health hazards.
risks.mitigation: Enforce strict asbestos management protocols in ESMPs for safe removal, packaging, transport, and disposal in compliance with NEMA guidelines.
risks.evidence: improper handling of asbestos cement (AC) pipes, OHS risks

risks.description: Delays by the Government of Uganda in making timely counterpart funding contributions for land acquisition and RAP compensations could stall civil works implementation.
risks.mitigation: Ensure GoU allocates adequate counterpart funds in annual sector budget allocations and track release schedules prior to contract execution.
risks.evidence: The GoU will be responsible for providing US$8 million in counterpart financing to cover... acquisition of land, and any compensation

risks.description: Inadequate coordination among multiple implementing departments, local authorities, and humanitarian agencies could lead to redundant infrastructure or improper site placement.
risks.mitigation: Utilize MWE's Sector Liaison Department for central coordination, engage a Project Support Team, and streamline planning through the Water and Environment Sector Working Group.
risks.evidence: In Uganda, a lack of coordination resulted in boreholes being drilled too close to each other or too close to shallow pit latrines

risks.description: Taking over management of financially unviable small towns with high operating costs could strain NWSC's cash flow and compromise capital investment capacity.
risks.mitigation: Apply standard due diligence assessments prior to town transfers, enforce automatic tariff indexation, and maintain a sustainable balance of grant and on-lending financing.
risks.evidence: The NWSC, however, is hesitant to take on additional debt given that its projected cash flow is earmarked for implementing a 10-year capital investment plan
